title: Missing Person UPDATE 3: Camille HILDERMAN Located Deceased
content:
Thirty-five year-old Camille HILDERMAN, who was the subject of a missing person investigation, has been located deceased.
HILDERMAN was last seen on Friday, June 5, 2026 in Wolseley, SK. It was believed she had travelled to Regina.
Following several days of investigation and searching, late yesterday afternoon (June 10, 2026), investigators located Hilderman, deceased, near Highway 11 northwest of Regina.
The investigation is now being led by RCMP with the assistance of the Regina Police Service.
Due to this death investigation being in its early stages, no further information is available at this time.
The Regina Police Service would like to thank the public, Regina Fire and Protective Services and the RCMP for their assistance in this ongoing investigation.

title: Investigation Underway Following Discovery of Human Remains
content:
The Regina Police Service, in conjunction with the Saskatchewan Coroners Service, have begun an investigation following the discovery of what appears to be human remains.
On June 9, 2026, at approximately 4:15 p.m., police were dispatched to a call for service on the 1300 block of Retallack Street. Upon arrival, officers located what appeared to be human remains outside a residence. Officers secured the area and requested additional resources from the Regina Police Service Major Crimes Unit, Regina Police Service Forensic Identification Unit and the Saskatchewan Coroners Service.
The death is considered suspicious however, at this early stage of the investigation, there are no further details that will be released to the public.
This investigation is
not
connected to the ongoing investigation of a missing 35 year-old woman.
Anyone who has information that could assist police in this investigation is asked to contact the Regina Police Service at 306-777-6500 or Regina Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477). The Regina Police Service thanks the public and the media for their assistance in this matter.

Twenty-three year-old Blaze LITTLECROW, is charged with:

title: Missing Person UPDATE: Regina Police Service and Regina Fire and Protective Services Conducting Search for 35 Year-Old Camille HILDERMAN
content:

Residents are asked to avoid the area while the search is carried out.

HILDERMAN is described as: female, 5’2”, weighing approximately 104 lbs. HILDERMAN has blonde and pink hair and brown eyes. She has piercings in her nose and lower lip. She has a tattoo on her upper left cheek bone, a triple seven tattoo on her cheek and a ghost on one of her inner arms. She was last seen wearing a black and white ruffled skirt with tights and a white and grey sweater. Photos of HILDERMAN accompany this release.
Anyone who has information that would help police locate Camille HILDERMAN is asked to contact the Regina Police Service at 306-777-6500 or Regina Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477).

title: Attempted Murder and Organized Crime Charges Laid
content:
Two adult males are facing charges in relation to an
investigation
that began in mid-April.
At approximately 1:50 a.m. on April 12, 2026, officers were patrolling in the area of Dewdney Avenue and Argyle Street when they observed an injured adult male on the sidewalk. The male was suffering from multiple lacerations. Officers provided first aid until EMS arrived and transported the male victim to hospital to be treated for, what appeared to be, serious injuries.
Investigators with the Regina Police Service Major Crimes Unit, Forensic Identification Unit and Canine Unit were called in to assist Patrol officers. Shortly after 2:00 a.m., the investigation led police to a residence in the 1400 block of Elphinstone Street where a search warrant was executed. Multiple people were located inside the home. Some were taken into custody on outstanding warrants.
Further investigation led police to arrest and charge two adult males in relation to this incident.
On Wednesday, June 10, 2026, 31 year-old Kenneth MANITOPYES was charged with:
Attempted Murder [CC 239]; and
Commission of an Offence for a Criminal Organization [CC 467.12].
MANITOPYES made his first appearance in Regina Provincial Court Thursday, June 11, 2026 at 9:30 a.m.
On Thursday, June 11, 37 year-old Chad KEEWATIN was charged with:
Attempted Murder- [CC 239]; and
Commission of an Offence for a Criminal Organization. [CC 467.12] and
Breach of Release Order [CC145(5)].
KEEWATIN will make his first appearance on these charges in Regina Provincial Court this morning, Friday June 12, 2026 at 9:30 a.m.

title: UPDATE: Request Assistance to Identify Human Remains
content:
The Regina Police Service is asking for assistance from the public to identify human remains buried outside a residence in the 1300 block of Retallack Street.
On June 9, 2026, at approximately 4:15 p.m., police were dispatched to a
call for service
on the 1300 block of Retallack Street. The caller told police they had discovered what appeared to be human remains buried outside the residence.
Over the course of a week, investigators with the Regina Police Service Major Crimes Unit, Regina Police Service Forensic Identification Unit, and the RCMP Historical Case Unit, methodically searched the area for evidence related to this suspicious death. Yesterday (June 16, 2026), the Saskatchewan Coroners Service conducted an autopsy which resulted in the discovery of the following information about the deceased:
Male
Approximately 5’9” tall
Between 30-40 years-old at the time of death
The remains have been buried in this location for a minimum of five years (prior to 2021).
At some point in his life, the male sustained a broken jaw that required surgical treatment.
At this time, there are no missing persons reported to the Regina Police Service who match this description. As such, we are appealing to the public to assist in identifying the deceased male.
Anyone who has information that could assist police in this investigation is asked to contact the Regina Police Service at 306-777-6500 or Regina Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477). The Regina Police Service thanks the public and the media for their assistance in this matter.

title: Investigation Underway Following Dog Attack
content:
The Regina Police Service and Animal Protection are investigating following a dog attack.
On June 17, 2026 at approximately 8:00 p.m., police were patrolling in the area of 6th
Avenue and Garnet Street when they were flagged down by two children. They told police they had been attacked by a dog. One child had a visible wound on his face. The victims also reported they witnessed the dog attack another dog in a nearby yard.

Animal Protection officers and police located the dog at a residence a short distance away. At this time, the dog is in the custody of Animal Protection. As per regular practice, Animal Protection has assumed the lead on this investigation and the Regina Police Service will assist as required.

title: Investigation Results in Significant Firearm and Drug Seizure
content:
Over 30 drug trafficking and firearms possession charges have been laid following a two-month investigation by the Regina Drug Unit (RDU).
On June 18, 2026, RDU investigators, with assistance from the RPS Tactical Support Unit, arrested a 43 year-old Regina man outside a residential complex in the 3200 block of Arens Road. A search of the suspect, subsequent to arrest, revealed the following:
A loaded 9mm handgun
A small amount of Canadian currency
Brass knuckles
A knife
Subsequent search warrants were executed in Regina on June 18, 2026. This included a residence in the 3200 block of Arens Road and two vehicles owned by the suspect. These searches resulted in the following items being located and seized:
4.2 kilograms of methamphetamine
Approximately .5 kg of fentanyl
3.82 grams of cocaine
The approximate street value of the drugs is $115,000.00. Investigators also seized:
$7,795.00 in Canadian currency
A second loaded 9mm handgun equipped with a “Glock switch” that rendered the firearm fully automatic
A loaded .22 calbre handgun equipped with a silencer
An SKS .762 semi-automatic rifle and ammunition
A .22 caliber AR semi-automatic rifle and ammunition
A 12-gauge shotgun and ammunition
Thousands of rounds of ammunition
Prohibited extended magazines
A variety of bladed weapons
Body armor and other tactical equipment
As a result, 43 year-old Andrew James PITTMAN of Regina was arrested and charged with:
3 x Possession of a Scheduled Substance for the Purpose of Trafficking [CDSA 5(2)];
Possession of the Proceeds of Property Obtained by Crime over $5000 [CC 355(a)];
2 x Careless Use of a Firearm [CC 86(2)];
5 x Possession of a Prohibited/Restricted Firearm with Ammunition [CC 95(1)];
3 x Possession of a Firearm Contrary to an Order [CC 117.01(1)];
Careless Use of a Firearm [CC 86(1)];
8 x Possession of a Device Knowing it’s Possession is Unauthorized [CC 92(2)];
3 x Unauthorized Possession of a Firearm in a Motor Vehicle [CC 94(1)]; and
3 x Tamper with the Serial Number of a Firearm [CC 108].
PITTMAN made his first appearance on these charges in Regina Provincial Court on June 19, 2026 at 9:30 a.m.
A third search warrant was executed on June 18, 2026 in Saskatoon. Members of the Saskatoon Police Service Crime Reduction Team and Tactical Support Unit executed the warrant at a residence in the 500 block of 5th
Avenue North in Saskatoon where one man was arrested and the following was seized;
$31,090.25 in Canadian currency
2016 Ford F-150
Cell phone
Assorted paraphernalia consistent with drug trafficking
As a result of this investigation, 32-year-old Chukwunonso Emmanuel OJUKWU of Saskatoon, SK is charged with:
Possession of the Proceeds of Property Obtained by Crime over $5000 [CC 355(a)]; and
Traffic in a Controlled Substance [CDSA 5(1)].
OJUKWU made his first appearance on these charges in Saskatoon Provincial Court on June 22, 2026.

title: Scam Warning: Traffic Violation Summons
content:
The Regina Police Service has received reports of scammers sending text messages claiming you must appear in court for an “unpaid traffic citation”. These messages often create urgency and pressure you into acting quickly.
What to watch for:
Messages stating you have an upcoming court date or you owe fines.
Threats of legal action, arrest or additional penalties.
A link directing you to “take action” to resolve the issue.
Requests for personal or financial information.
What to do:
Do not click the link.
Do not provide any personal or payment information.
If you believe you have an outstanding traffic citation, you can verify by calling the Regina Traffic Safety Court.

title: 2026 Canada Day Celebrations
content:
Let’s celebrate Canada Day safely. On Wednesday, July 1, 2026, Wascana Park will be filled with a variety of events and entertainment. The day kicks off with a pancake breakfast and wraps up with a fireworks display after sunset (approximately 10:30 p.m.). For full event details, visit
https://www.reginacanadaday.ca/
.
Officers from our Traffic Safety Unit, Public Safety Unit and Patrol will be on hand throughout the day making sure everyone is safe. This includes the closure of Albert Street between College Avenue and 20th
Avenue to all vehicle traffic beginning at 8:30 p.m.
The Regina Police Service reminds drivers that parking illegally or stopping your vehicle on any road to watch the fireworks is not allowed. Officers will be ensuring that the rules of the road are being followed to ensure everyone’s safety.
Safety and Etiquette Reminders:
Expect increased vehicle and pedestrian traffic near Wascana Park. Plan your route, leave early and be patient and respectful.
Park only in designated spots, lock your doors and remove valuables.
Smoking is not permitted in public areas.
Dispose of trash properly and consume alcohol only in the designated beer garden.
Take a photo of your child before arriving in case you become separated during the event.
If you lose or find a child, go to the Lost Children’s Tent near the Main Stage off Legislative Drive.
Consider getting a *Next to Kin tag for your child or family member when you arrive at the event.
Be mindful of other events happening in the park and respect those activities.
*Next to Kin Tag:
The Next to Kin Tag is a safety tool that can help reunite families when someone becomes separated in crowded settings. The tap-enabled tag can be attached to clothing or a keychain and is easily scanned with a smartphone to display parent or guardian contact information.
Next to Kin tags are available free-of-charge at the Lost Children’s Tent.
For more information about Next to Kin, visit their website: www.nexttokin.ca.
Have a safe and happy Canada Day!

content:

title: SIRT Investigating Officer-Involved Shooting
content:

The
Saskatchewan Police Act, 1990, the Saskatchewan Serious Incident Response Team (*SIRT) is now investigating an officer-involved, non-fatal shooting that occurred early this morning in Regina.
At approximately 2:10 a.m. police were called to a residence in the 800 block of Elphinstone Street for a report of an adult male discharging a crossbow and threatening occupants inside the residence.

We understand this incident is of public interest and ask for patience as the facts are gathered. Because this is an active SIRT investigation, no further information will be provided by the Regina Police Service. Additional information will be provided by SIRT as it becomes available.

SIRT
.

is an independent, civilian-led organization responsible for investigating serious incidents involving police officers in Saskatchewan.

title: Four Charged Following Retail Theft Enforcement Project
content:
Four people are facing charges following a one-day targeted enforcement project by the Regina Police Service (RPS).
On June 25, 2026, officers with the RPS Criminal Investigation Unit, Property Crimes Unit and Robbery Unit teamed up to identify and arrest shoplifters at three businesses – two in the 2000 block of Prince of Wales Drive and one in the 2100 block of Prince of Wales Drive.
The suspects were arrested outside the locations after they were observed leaving the business without paying for items in their possession. Stolen items included various grocery and household products. One of the four suspects was arrested for failure to comply with probation.
The public can expect to hear more about this type of targeted enforcement as the Service renews its focus on retail theft enforcement through the Retail Theft Strategy.
Retail Theft Strategy
The Regina Police Service has a multi-pronged approach to tackling retail theft in our city, including identifying ongoing crime trends, locations, and repeat offenders. Business owners are encouraged to invest in security cameras, if possible, and always report theft to police, using the
Direct Entry Victim Reporting system (DEVRS).
All files are reviewed and offenders are held to account when investigations support criminal charges. The Regina Police Service takes retail theft seriously and, although much of the work takes place after the occurrence, collaborative crime prevention is a key component.

title: Weapons Investigation Results in Multiple Charges
content:
An adult male and adult female are charged following a weapons offence that resulted in injuries to a 36 year-old woman. A patrol officer was also assaulted during the course of the investigation.
On Saturday, July 11, 2026, at approximately 7:00 a.m., officers were called to the 800 block of Elphinstone Street for a report of a weapons offence involving a knife. Based on information gathered, the first officer on scene conducted a traffic stop on a taxi in the 1100 block of Elphinstone Street. The officer approached the vehicle to speak with the female passenger believed to be involved in the incident.
While speaking with the female, a male approached the officer in a threatening manner and was interfering with the investigation. The officer directed the male to sit down until he was finished speaking with the female. The male suspect did not comply. The officer then informed him that he was under arrest for obstructing an investigation and attempted to take him into custody. The male suspect resisted arrest and assaulted the officer. Additional Patrol units arrived on scene and officers took the male into custody. The officer who was assaulted was assessed and treated for minor injuries.
Further investigation determined that the incident stemmed from an altercation that occurred approximately one hour earlier at a residence on Rothwell Street. Witnesses told officers that a female, later located by officers in the taxicab, arrived at the residence and knocked on the door. When a 36 year-old female answered, she was stabbed by the female suspect, who then fled the scene. Following the incident, the victim and the male, who was later arrested for assaulting a police officer, left the residence on Rothwell Street for another residence in the 1100 block of Elphinstone Street. A short time later, the 31 year-old female suspect arrived at that address where a second altercation occurred involving the female suspect, the victim and two other individuals.
Police were called a short time later. The 36 year-old female victim was taken to hospital by EMS to be treated for, what appeared to be, a minor stab wound.
All involved were known to each other.
As a result of this investigation, a 31 year-old female is charged with:
Assault with a Weapon [CC 266]; and
Fail to Comply with Probation Order [CC 733.1(1)].
The 31 year-old will make her first appearance on these charges in Regina Provincial Court August 31, 2026.
A 40 year-old male is charged with:
Assault A Peace Officer [CC 270(1)(A)]; and
Obstruction [CC 129(A)].
The 40 year-old male will make his first appearance on these charges in Regina Provincial Court on August 31, 2026.

content:
The Regina Police Service is encouraged by the release of the latest national crime statistics, which show continued improvements in community safety.
According to Statistics Canada’s annual police-reported crime data, released today (July 22, 2026), the *Crime Severity Index (CSI) and overall *Crime Rate both decreased by 12 per cent from 2024 to 2025 for the Regina area. Regina now ranks 13th among 41 *Census Metropolitan Areas (CMAs) for both Crime Severity Index and overall Crime Rate, with improvements recorded in both violent and non-violent crime severity.
These results represent some of the city’s lowest crime rankings in recent years.
“In 2016 our city was number one,” explains Chief Lorilee Davies. “To have made this much progress in just under a decade is something we should be proud of and shows our multi-faceted approach to enforcement, crime prevention and community partnerships is making a meaningful difference.”
The Regina Police Service also saw a 14 per cent increase in its *Clearance Rate, demonstrating continued success in identifying offenders, advancing investigations and holding those responsible for crimes accountable.
Across Canada, crime declined for the second consecutive year. Nationally, the CSI, violent crime and non-violent crime all decreased. Significant reductions were also reported in break and enters, motor vehicle thefts and homicides.
Although Saskatchewan continues to report the highest Crime Severity Index and Crime Rate among the provinces, both measures declined by five per cent over the previous year, reinforcing the importance of continued collaborative efforts to improve public safety.
“The Regina CMA numbers reflect the dedication of officers, civilian professionals, and community partners,” says Chief Lorilee Davies. “Through data-driven initiatives like our Aerial Support Unit, the focus on downtown presence and Community ON Crime Prevention programs, we are all contributing to a safer city.”
The Regina Police Service will continue to use crime data and evidence-based policing strategies to guide operational priorities, strengthen community partnerships, and address the issues that matter most to Regina residents.
Read the full Statistics Canada report
here
.
*The “Crime Severity Index” accounts for the seriousness of crime by “weighting” crime types based on conviction rates and lengths of sentences – a homicide therefore has a much greater effect on the CSI than a single theft. However, high-volume, low-severity crime types can still have a substantial impact on the CSI.
*The “Crime Rate” is a measure of the number of crimes per 100,000 population. Using this measure enables comparisons of crime counts over time and between regions.
*The “Clearance Rate” refers to the number of criminal incidents solved by the police in the year divided by the number of criminal incidents reported in the year. Police can clear an incident by charge or by means other than the laying of a charge.
*What is a Census Metropolitan Area?
Source: Statistics Canada, Map: Regina [Census metropolitan area], Saskatchewan
A CMA refers to an urban core and its surrounding area (based on commuting patterns) with a total population of 100,000 or more and at least 50,000 people residing within the urban core itself. Some CMAs have populations that reside primarily within the urban core while other CMAs have populations that are more dispersed among a number of surrounding communities.
CMAs typically cover more than one police jurisdiction. The Regina CMA (outlined in blue) is policed by the Regina Police Service within the city limits, and by additional RCMP detachments for the largely rural area surrounding the City of Regina. The Regina CMA includes communities such as: White City, Pilot Butte, Balgonie, Lumsden, Regina Beach, Pense, and Belle Plaine.

title: Over $3900 in Traffic Tickets Issued Following Incident of Youths Driving E-Bikes Dangerously
content:
Three male youths, ages 12, 13 and 14 were issued over $3,900 in traffic tickets after refusing to stop for police while riding e-dirtbikes/e-scooter at high speeds through the streets and pathways of northwest Regina. The RPS Aerial Support Unit eventually tracked the youth to their residences.
The incident began at approximately 8:00 p.m. on Wednesday, July 22, 2026. An officer with the Traffic Safety Unit was patrolling in the area of Lakeridge Road and Rochdale Blvd. when they observed four youth, three were riding e-dirtbikes and the fourth was on an e-scooter. The youth were not complying with the rules of the road. The officer activated his emergency lights and attempted to pull them over, but the youth did not stop. Officers on the ground alerted the Aerial Support Unit (ASU), which was quickly able to get a visual on the youth as they fled into a green space in the area. ASU directed the two officers on the ground to the greenspace. Three of the youth fled when they saw police. The fourth remained and spoke to police.
A short time later, police attended to the residences of all three youth. Each was issued $1,310 in traffic fines.
The Regina Police Service would like to remind all residents of the rules regarding e-bikes and e-scooters. More information can be found on our website.

title: ADVISORY: RPS SWAT Team Training at Regina General Hospital
content:
Beginning at 9:30 a.m. this morning, (Thursday, July 23, 2026), the Regina Police Service SWAT team will be on site outside the Regina General Hospital (RGH) for a training exercise. The training will include rappel work. Those in the area may see officers on top of and around the building. Multiple police vehicle will also be parked in the area.
This training location is a healthcare facility. As such, members of the media and the public are required to refrain from taking pictures and filming this training. The air space above and around the RGH is completely restricted in order to ensure the safety of the operation of the STARS helicopter. Please do not operate drones in or near this area. This includes the safety of the staff, patients and those in the area.
Consistent, collaborative training with our community partners and stakeholders is important to ensure everyone is prepared and knows what their role is in the case of a real emergency. We thank the Regina General Hospital, the Saskatchewan Health Authority and our many other community partners for working with us to help keep our community safe.

title: Public Safety Alert: Male Subject, High Risk to Reoffend
content:
Under the authority of, and pursuant to, the Saskatchewan Public Disclosure Act, the Regina Police Service is issuing a public advisory on a male, who is considered to be a high risk to reoffend sexually. As of today, 49 year-old Jason Paul THORN will reside in the Heritage neighbourhood of Regina in a residence that provides supervision and monitoring of his activities.
This information is intended to enable members of the public to take suitable preventative measures, not to embark upon any form of vigilantism or other unreasonable conduct directed at this individual.
Jason Paul THORN is described as: Male, 49 years old, 5‘ 9” tall, weighing approximately 170 pounds, medium build, with brown eyes and black hair. A recent photo of THORN accompanies this release.
A brief description of THORN’s offending behavior is as follows: Jason Paul THORN has a criminal history which includes sexual offences and has a history of reoffending. He poses a high risk for acts of sexual offending against female children. The prospects for reduction of his risk through treatment interventions are poor.
Jason Paul THORN will be released on his legislated Statutory Release effective July 27 and will resume his Long-Term Supervision Order on March 18, 2027.
THORN must abide by the following Parole Board of Canda imposed special conditions:
Follow a treatment plan/program to be arranged by his parole supervisor in the areas of sexual deviancy, trauma and substance abuse.
Follow a psychological counselling plan to be arranged by your parole supervisor/as directed by a clinician in relation to sexual deviancy.
Follow a psychiatric counselling and medication regime as directed by a clinician.
Abstain from consuming, purchasing or possessing alcohol or any drugs not prescribed. Over the counter drugs must be taken as recommended by the manufacturer.
Not to associate with any person known to be, or have reason to believe to be, involved in criminal activity or substance use
Immediately report all intimate sexual and nonsexual relationships and friendships or changes in relationships to his parole supervisor.
Not to purchase, acquire, possess or access pornography or sexually explicit material in any form or type of media.
Not to be in the presence of any children under the age of 18 unless he is accompanied by a responsible adult who knows his criminal history and has previously been approved in writing, by the parole supervisor.
Not to be in, near, or around places where children under the age of 18 are likely to congregate such as elementary and secondary schools, parks, swimming pools and recreational centres unless accompanied by an adult previously approved in writing by his parole supervisor.
Reside at a designated community-based residential facility or psychiatric facility approved by the Correctional Service of Canada.
Any member of the public who has questions or concerns is encouraged to contact the Regina Police Service at 306-777-6500. Any person who wishes to report an incident where Jason Paul THORN is in violation of the aforementioned conditions, should call the Regina Police Service at 306-777-6500 or Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-8477 (TIPS). Concerns or reports from persons living outside of Regina should be directed to the nearest detachment of the RCMP or local municipal police department.
This information is intended to raise community awareness about the presence of this offender so that people may make informed choices about contact with this person. This information is not to be used for an unlawful purpose.

title: One Charged Following Offence Involving Machete
content:
A 37 year-old male is facing charges following a weapons-related incident involving a machete.
At approximately 4:40 p.m. on Saturday, July 25, 2026, police were dispatched to the 1000 block of Angus Street following a report of a weapons offence. Upon arrival, officers located an injured male who reported that the suspect attempted to steal his bicycle before assaulting him. EMS transported the victim to hospital for, what appeared to be, significant but non-life-threatening injuries.
Officers subsequently located the suspect at a nearby residence and took him into custody without incident. Following the arrest, officers executed a search of the residence and seized a machete believed to be connected to the incident.
As a result of this investigation, 37 year-old Dylan SHEEPSKIN is charged with the following:
Aggravated Assault [CC 268(1)]; and
Robbery [CC 344(1)(B)].
SHEEPSKIN made his first appearance on these charges in Regina Provincial Court this morning (July 27, 2026).

title: One Charged Following Dangerous Drive
content:
At approximately 1:00 a.m. on Monday, July 27, 2026, members of the Regina Police Service attempted to conduct a traffic stop in the 1300 block of Robinson Street. The driver failed to stop and fled at a high rate of speed.
The Regina Police Service Aerial Support Unit monitored the vehicle as it travelled through Regina and eastbound on Highway 1 toward Moose Jaw at excessive speeds. Members of the Moose Jaw Police Service assisted by attempting to deploy a tire deflation device; however, the driver turned around before reaching the device and returned toward Regina.
As the vehicle re-entered the city, Regina Police Service officers successfully deployed a tire deflation device. The vehicle continued for a short distance before slowing and coming to a stop, at which point officers conducted a high-risk traffic stop. The lone male driver was arrested without incident.
As a result of this investigation, 34 year-old Tyler LAVALLEE is charged with:
Operate Conveyance Dangerous to Public [CT 320.13(1)];
Flight from Peace Officer [CT 320.17]; and
Unlawfully at Large [CC 145(1)].
LAVALLEE made his first appearance on these charges in Regina Provincial Court this morning (July 27, 2026) at 9:30 a.m.

title: One Charged Following Assault Investigation
content:
On July 26, 2026, at approximately 1:00 a.m., patrolling officers responded to the 1100 block of Cameron Street after receiving a report of an assault in progress.
Upon arrival, officers located an injured adult male lying in the roadway. During the investigation, officers determined that the injured male was the suspect in an earlier assault on an adult female.
The investigation revealed that the suspect had allegedly assaulted the female victim before being confronted by an adult male who intervened. An altercation then occurred between the two males, resulting in the suspect sustaining injuries.
The suspect was taken into custody at the scene and treated by EMS before being transported to hospital for further assessment. Officers located a pipe that had been used as a weapon during the assault.
As a result of this investigation, 27 year-old Braydon LAVALLEE is charged with:
Sexual Assault with a Weapon [CC 272(1)(A)]; and
Assault with a Weapon [CC 267(A)].
LAVALLEE made his first appearance on these charges in Regina Provincial Court this morning (July 27, 2026) at 9:30 a.m.

title: ADVISORY: Collaborative Joint Training Exercise at the Regina International Airport
content:
This afternoon (Tuesday, July 28, 2026), the Regina Police Service Tactical Support Team will collaborate with the Regina Airport Authority, Regina Fire and Protective Services and Regina Emergency Medical Services (EMS) for a joint training exercise at the Regina International Airport. The training will explore several different public safety scenarios specific to the location.
Officers will be on-site starting at 11:30 a.m. The training exercise will last until approximately 2:00 p.m. Those in the area can expect to see multiple first response vehicles parked outside the location for the duration of the training event.
Consistent, collaborative training with our community’s first responders and partners is important to ensure everyone is prepared and knows what their role is in the case of a real emergency. We would like to thank the Regina Airport Authority and our many other community partners for working with us to help keep our community safe.
